core_obligations: Given two presentations alpha : R[x_1, ..., x_n] -> A and beta : R[y_1, ..., y_m] -> A, choose f_j in R[x_1, ..., x_n] with alpha(f_j) = beta(y_j) and g_i in R[y_1, ..., y_m] with beta(g_i) = alpha(x_i) (proof lines 21308-21311).
Assemble the displayed commutative diagram with corners the polynomial ring in both sets of variables, the two single polynomial rings, and A (proof lines 21312-21320).

Show that after a change of coordinates the map R[x_1, ..., x_n, y_1, ..., y_m] -> R[x_1, ..., x_n] is isomorphic to the one mapping each y_i to zero, and similarly for the left vertical map (proof lines 21321-21324).
Conclude by induction on the number of variables that the lemma follows from the add-a-variable pseudo-coherence statement (proof lines 21325-21326).
Deduce the pseudo-coherent case from the m-pseudo-coherent case together with the relation between m-pseudo-coherence and pseudo-coherence (proof lines 21327-21328).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a finite type ring map R -> A, a complex K^bullet of A-modules, and an integer m, and establishes the equivalence of two conditions: that for some presentation alpha : R[x_1, ..., x_n] -> A the complex K^bullet be an m-pseudo-coherent complex of R[x_1, ..., x_n]-modules, and that the same hold for all presentations; it adds that the same equivalence holds for pseudo-coherence (source lines 21290-21305). The proof is a comparison-of-presentations argument. Given two presentations alpha and beta, the proof chooses f_j in R[x_1, ..., x_n] with alpha(f_j) = beta(y_j) and g_i in R[y_1, ..., y_m] with beta(g_i) = alpha(x_i), and assembles the displayed commutative diagram whose corners are the polynomial ring in both sets of variables, the two polynomial rings, and A (proof lines 21307-21320). The substantive step is the normalisation: after a change of coordinates, the ring homomorphism R[x_1, ..., x_n, y_1, ..., y_m] -> R[x_1, ..., x_n] becomes isomorphic to the one mapping each y_i to zero, and similarly for the left vertical map of the diagram; hence by induction on the number of variables the lemma follows from the add-a-variable statement for pseudo-coherence (proof lines 21321-21326). The pseudo-coherent case is then obtained from this together with the passage between m-pseudo-coherence and pseudo-coherence (proof lines 21327-21328). The non-routine content is the coordinate change that normalises an arbitrary comparison map to one killing the extra variables.
